primary.poolable_reason: THIS IS THE CLOSEST OF THE SEVEN TO POOLABLE, AND IT STILL IS NOT. Both trials test etripamil against placebo in paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia -- intervention, comparator and population all match, which is rare in this set. But the registered primaries are different KINDS of quantity: NCT02296190 registers 'The Percentage of Subjects Successfully Converted From PSVT to Sinus Rhythm Within 15 Minutes' -- a proportion at a fixed time -- and NCT03464019 registers 'The Time to Conversion of an Episode of PSVT to Sinus Rhythm' -- a time-to-event. A proportion and a survival time are not two measurements of one estimand, and converting between them requires assumptions neither registration supports. THIS IS THE TOPIC MOST WORTH REVISITING if a common outcome is reported in both publications.

primary.what_this_verdict_does_not_establish: NOT that any of these trials is poor -- each is registered, randomised where it says so, and reports its primary. NOT that the drug is ineffective. NOT that no poolable question exists in this area: only that the question this page's title asks cannot be answered by pooling the trials this page carries. If a further eligible trial is identified, this verdict should be revisited.

risk_of_bias_verdict: Not assessed. A risk-of-bias assessment grades trials contributing to a pooled result, and this page publishes none.
